title: Choose bldr's visual world
question: The roll assigned Registrar Carbon Copy. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Registrar Carbon Copy
options.lineage: KU enrollment worksheets and carbon-copy add/drop slips
options.thesis: Every schedule is one sheet in a carbon-copy pad: flip the top copy and the next combination is underneath.
options.viewport: A full-width enrollment worksheet: headline as the form title, weekly grid as the form body, copies stacked beneath with 'Copy 3 of 47'. A real guest button sits in the signature box.
options.risk: Reads bureaucratic if set timidly; needs bold display type and full canary/pink fields to feel warm.

raised.raise: Visible count as record: a stamped tally ('47 schedules fit') updates as the pad flips.
Real depth: white, canary and pink copies are stacked, offset planes; the top sheet lifts away.
Total colour commitment: canary and pink carbon own whole sections, not accent chips.
Fading history: the previous schedule stays a faint carbon impression for a beat after each flip.

options.label: Fieldhouse Gameday Program
options.lineage: Allen Fieldhouse programs, scoreboards and hardwood
options.thesis: Picking classes as picking a lineup: the scoreboard counts schedules, the program lists your starting five.
options.viewport: Hardwood ground with a scoreboard reading SCHEDULE 03 / 47; your five classes listed as a starting lineup beside it.
options.risk: Familiar: sports theming is where most KU-flavoured projects go, and it can tip into costume.

options.label: Two-ink Riso
options.lineage: Riso zines and Lawrence gig posters
options.thesis: Crimson and blue spot inks misregister over paper; each schedule is another print from the same plate.
options.viewport: Huge two-ink headline over a blue-printed calendar with crimson class blocks overprinting; inks shift on each new combination.
options.case: Students identify with the poster culture; loses on clarity because grain fights a dense time grid.
options.risk: Riso texture is a popular look and could read as trend-chasing.

options.label: Split-flap Departures
options.thesis: Your week as a departures board: each class is a row, and the flaps cascade to the next schedule.
options.viewport: A full-width board: class, days, time and building flipping character by character through combinations.
options.case: The flap cascade makes 'browse every schedule' very clear; loses on audience identification (not KU, not warm).
options.risk: A dark board drifts back toward the black UI being replaced.

options.label: Cereal Box Aisle
options.thesis: Schedules as boxes on a shelf.
options.viewport: A planogram wall of schedule boxes.
options.case: Loses both axes: no KU link, and boxes hide the weekly grid.

options.label: Matchbook Drawer
options.thesis: Each schedule as a pocketable cover.
options.case: Loses both axes: nightlife nostalgia, and covers can't show a week.
options.kept: A visible count kept as a record.

options.label: Multiplane Dawn
options.thesis: Painted planes sliding at different speeds.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to scheduling or KU.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.case: Loses both axes and is the neon-on-black look being removed.
options.kept: Fading history of the previous state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light product page in the Notion Calendar / Linear mould, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and guest button over a full-width, unframed calendar showing a generated schedule.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
